docs.title: BerEditor: ASN.1, BER/DER, and KMIP TTLV Workbench
docs.text:
BerEditor is a desktop utility for inspecting and working with encoded data used in ASN.1-based protocols and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). Its main window presents BER data as a navigable structure, while related tools support data conversion, certificate and key operations, cryptographic tasks, and KMIP TTLV messages.

This overview follows the feature set described by the BerEditor project page and the application menus and implementations in the source code. Menu availability can depend on the installed license.

docs.title: Main window
docs.text: The main window is the starting point for opening and navigating encoded data. The screenshot below shows the BerEditor interface with a decoded structure displayed in the central view.

docs.title: What BerEditor is for
docs.text:
ASN.1 defines data types and structures; BER (Basic Encoding Rules) and DER (Distinguished Encoding Rules) encode those structures as bytes. The bytes themselves can be difficult to interpret by eye. BerEditor decodes supported BER/DER data into a tree so that the structure and values can be examined, and provides tools to create, edit, compare, and validate encoded data.

The application also recognizes KMIP TTLV (Tag, Type, Length, Value), the message encoding used by the Key Management Interoperability Protocol. TTLV has its own tree and tools in BerEditor; it is related to the application's data-inspection workflow but is not BER or DER.

docs.title: Inspect and edit BER/DER
docs.text:
Open BER-encoded files and inspect their nodes in the main tree view. Selecting a node lets you work with its value and encoded data. The application includes commands to decode BER, create BER, check BER data, compare two BER values, and retrieve BER data from a URI. BER editing and several auxiliary viewing tabs are license-controlled.

For common PKI objects, the application offers dedicated views and tools for certificates, certificate signing requests (CSRs), certificate revocation lists (CRLs), keys, and CMS/PKCS#7 data. Dedicated information dialogs expose fields in a more meaningful form than raw bytes alone.

docs.title: Work with alternate data representations
docs.text: The tool menu includes a data converter for encoding or converting input data, a BER decoding tool, a BER construction tool, and a numeric converter. Depending on the selected data and license, BerEditor also provides XML, text, and log views alongside the structured representation. These views are useful when investigating how an encoded object relates to readable or application-level data.

docs.title: Inspect ASN.1 object identifiers
docs.text: The OID Information tool looks up object identifier values used in ASN.1, certificates, and cryptographic formats. This helps identify algorithm, extension, and attribute identifiers encountered while inspecting PKI data.

docs.title: Use KMIP TTLV tools
docs.text: The KMIP menu provides separate functions to decode TTLV, create TTLV, encode TTLV, and interact with a KMIP server through the TTLV client. Decoded TTLV data is shown as a structured tree, making nested request and response messages easier to inspect. The source also detects TTLV input and can offer to open it in the TTLV view; TTLV decoding requires a license.

docs.title: PKI and cryptographic utilities
docs.text:
BerEditor groups cryptographic operations and certificate-related tools in its Cryptogram and Service menus. The source includes workflows for key generation and management, certificate and CSR handling, signing and verification, encryption and decryption, hashing and MAC generation, OTP generation, and big-number calculations. Other certificate utilities include certificate path validation and X.509 comparison. An SSL Check tool inspects SSL/TLS connections or protocol support, and an ACME client is available for certificate automation workflows.

These are practical tools for development and troubleshooting. Their presence does not by itself establish that a particular certificate, key, connection, or cryptographic configuration is secure; results depend on the supplied data, configuration, and validation context.

docs.title: Examine an encoded object
docs.text:
1. Open a BER/DER file in BerEditor.
  2. Expand the tree to navigate through the ASN.1 structure.
  3. Select a node to inspect its value or encoded bytes.
  4. Use the relevant information dialog, OID lookup, or alternate view to interpret the fields.
  5. If needed, compare the data with another BER object or run the BER check tool.

docs.title: Construct or convert data
docs.text: Use the data converter when starting with input that should be encoded, and the BER creation tool when assembling BER data. Decode the resulting bytes in the main viewer to inspect their structure. Available operations and editing controls may depend on the license.

docs.title: Inspect a KMIP message
docs.text: Open a TTLV message with the TTLV decoder or use the KMIP client/encoder workflow. Navigate the decoded Tag, Type, Length, and Value items in the TTLV tree, then use the encoder or client tool as appropriate for the next step.

docs.title: Review PKI material
docs.text: Open a certificate, CSR, CRL, or key in the corresponding BerEditor workflow. Use the dedicated information dialogs for its fields, OID Information for identifiers, Certificate Path Validation for a chain-validation task, and X.509 Compare to compare certificates. Use signing, verification, encryption, or decryption tools when the task requires those operations.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text: The project page identifies the following as available in both licensed and unlicensed editions: BER/DER viewing, data encoding, the numeric converter, and OID information. It lists XML, text, and log tabs; cryptographic menu functions; BER editing; SSL Check; Certificate Path Validation; KMIP TTLV; X.509 Compare; and the ACME client as licensed-edition features. Exact feature availability should be confirmed against the version and license in use.

docs.title: Platforms, downloads, and support
docs.text:
The project page lists installers or packages for Windows 64-bit, macOS, and Linux 64-bit. The links below are the version 2.9.6 downloads listed on that page:

  • BerEditor 2.9.6 for Windows 64-bit
  • BerEditor 2.9.6 for macOS

The project page describes the download size as approximately 35 MB; actual size may vary by platform and release. Check the project page for newer releases.

docs.title: Viewing ASN.1 BER/DER Data with BerEditor
docs.text:
BerEditor can decode ASN.1 data encoded with BER or DER and display its structure and values. This is useful when examining X.509 certificates, certificate revocation lists (CRLs), private keys, and other ASN.1-based data.

This guide is adapted from the original BerEditor article. The screenshots below use the corresponding images included with this project.

docs.title: Ways to load encoded data
docs.text:
BerEditor provides several ways to open data:

  1. Open a file from the File > Open menu.
  2. Paste hexadecimal or Base64 data into the BER decoder.
  3. Drag and drop a BER/DER binary or PEM file into the application.
  4. Retrieve data from a URI using Tool > Get BER from URI.

docs.title: Open a file
docs.text: Choose File > Open, then select a BER or DER binary file. PEM-encoded files can also be opened; BerEditor recognizes common input encodings automatically.

docs.title: Enter BER data directly
docs.text: Choose Tool > Decode BER and enter the data as hexadecimal or Base64 text. The example below shows the decoder dialog with hexadecimal input.

docs.title: Drag and drop a file
docs.text: You can also drag a BER/DER binary file or a PEM file from your file manager and drop it into BerEditor. The decoded data opens in the main viewer.

docs.title: Retrieve data from a URI
docs.text: Choose Tool > Get BER from URI to retrieve encoded data from a network address. For HTTP, BerEditor issues a GET request and treats the response body as binary data. For LDAP, it connects to the LDAP address and retrieves data using the specified filter and data type.

docs.title: Reading the decoded data
docs.text:
The viewer organizes decoded data into three main areas:

  • BER tree: the hierarchical ASN.1 structure.
  • Hex view: the encoded bytes, with multiple display modes.
  • Selected-item details: information about the node selected in the BER tree.

BerEditor detects common input forms such as binary BER/DER, PEM, and Base64. The right-hand pane also provides tabs for viewing data as Hex, XML, Text, and JSON.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Use file opening, direct data entry, drag and drop, or URI retrieval to load BER/DER data. Then navigate the tree, inspect the encoded bytes, and use the alternate views to understand the decoded structure.

docs.title: BerEditor Features by License Status
docs.text: This page summarizes the feature differences between the unlicensed and licensed versions of BerEditor. It reflects the application menus and license checks in the source code; available actions can also vary by build and platform.

docs.text: Area Without a license With a license BER files Open and inspect BER data in the main tree, subject to the 10,000-byte unlicensed limit. Open larger BER files. BER operations Decode BER. docs.text: BerEditor labels the unlicensed application in its window title and About dialog. You can review license status and request, import, update, or renew a license from the License Information interface. The application includes a free-license request flow; check the current in-app instructions for eligibility and request details. Restart BerEditor when prompted to apply a changed license.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• A license unlocks application features; it does not guarantee that a particular operation will succeed. Results still depend on input data, configuration, and the relevant protocol or cryptographic requirements.
  • This document describes the license gates present in the codebase. Consult the documentation or the running version for any release-specific changes.

docs.title: Install BerEditor on macOS
docs.text:
1. Open the downloaded BerEditor disk image (.dmg). A window like the one below will appear.
  1. Click and hold the BerEditor icon.
  2. Drag it onto the Applications folder icon, then release the mouse button.
  3. Wait for the copy to finish, then eject the BerEditor disk image.
  4. Open Applications and double-click BerEditor to launch it.

If macOS asks you to confirm that you want to open the app, review the prompt and choose Open.

docs.title: ACME Client Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The ACME Client communicates with an ACME directory to manage an account, create certificate orders, complete authorizations, and retrieve issued certificates. It exposes individual ACME commands and a guided Issue Certificate workflow.

Figure 1. ACME Client dialog. Retrieve the directory first to populate endpoint commands, then build and send requests while parsing server responses.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Use CertMan — Select whether the ACME account key comes from CertMan or KeyPairMan. The client supports RSA, ECDSA, and EdDSA account keys.
  2. ACME URL / Directory / Clear — Enter the ACME directory URL and select Directory to retrieve its endpoint map. The command selector is populated from the directory response. Clear clears saved URL entries.
  3. Cert ID / Issue Certificate — Cert ID identifies a certificate for applicable commands. Issue Certificate runs the guided account, order, authorization, challenge, finalize, and certificate retrieval sequence, prompting before each step.
  4. Link tab — Contains Nonce URL, Location, and KID. Get Nonce fetches a Replay-Nonce; GetLocation retrieves the selected resource; Get PubKey loads the account key's public-key identifier. Nonce automatic change allows the nonce to be refreshed during command processing.
  5. User tab — Enter the account Email and add DNS identifiers to the DNS list. DNS Check opens DNS checking for the listed names. Add and Clear manage the identifier list. ChallTest opens the challenge test utility.
  6. Command tab — Select an ACME command, enter or confirm its endpoint URL, and choose Make to create the signed JSON request. The hash selection is used with the account key.
  7. Auth List / Challenge List / Order List — Display parsed authorizations, challenges, and orders. Their context menus provide available row operations, including removal or rebuilding where supported.
  8. Method / Auto Send / Send — Choose POST or GET. Auto Send transmits a generated request automatically; otherwise use Send manually.
  9. Thumb Print / Deactivate / UpdateAccount — Run account/key actions for the selected ACME context.
  10. Request — Displays the JSON/JWS request. Verify checks its JWS signature; View opens the JSON structure; C clears it. HTTP Status shows the response status associated with the request exchange.
  11. Response / Parser / Auto / Status — Displays the server's JSON or Base64 response. Parser interprets the response and updates command, authorization, challenge, or order lists. Auto parses responses automatically. View inspects the response structure; C clears it.
  12. Clear All / Close — Clear the current ACME state or close the dialog.

docs.title: Start an ACME Session
docs.text:
1. Enter the ACME directory URL and select Directory. The directory endpoints and nonce URL are loaded into the command controls.
  2. Select an account key source with Use CertMan. The first signed request prompts for the account key pair or certificate/key from the selected manager.
  3. Select Get Nonce or leave Nonce automatic change enabled to manage nonces during requests.
  4. Enter the account email in the User tab and add the DNS identifier to the list.
  5. Choose a command and review the endpoint URL. Select Make to build the signed request. With Auto Send enabled, it is sent immediately.
  6. Review the HTTP status and response. Keep Auto enabled or select Parser to extract endpoint links and populate the command, authorization, challenge, and order lists.

docs.title: Issue a Certificate
docs.text:
1. Retrieve the directory and nonce, enter the account email, and add one DNS name. The guided workflow currently supports one DNS identifier at a time.
  2. Select Issue Certificate and confirm each prompted command. The workflow creates an account and order, processes authorization and challenge steps, finalizes the order, fetches the order/certificate, and displays the returned certificate chain.
  3. Complete the DNS or HTTP challenge with the validation data required by the ACME server. Use DNS Check or ChallTest where appropriate; this dialog does not make control of the domain automatic.
  4. When prompted, save the issued certificate and private key to CertMan.

docs.title: Command and Response Handling
docs.text:
• Directory fetches the server's directory object and fills the endpoint list.
  • Make constructs the request for the selected command; Send transmits it using the selected HTTP method.
  • Parser reads the response status and detail, then adds links for related operations such as finalize, authorization, orders, and certificate retrieval.
  • GetLocation retrieves a resource URL; UpdateAccount and Deactivate run the corresponding account commands.
  • Right-click rows in the command, authorization, challenge, or order lists for supported row actions.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• ACME requires a reachable directory endpoint, valid account credentials, fresh replay nonces, and successful domain authorization.
  • Keep the ACME account private key confidential. Changing account keys or deactivating an account affects the server-side ACME account.
  • Review the server response and HTTP status after every operation. A successful request submission does not mean domain authorization or certificate issuance succeeded.
  • Challenge validation may require DNS or web-server configuration outside BerEditor. Complete that step before finalizing the order.

docs.title: BER Format Check Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The BER format check dialog checks whether BER-encoded data matches a supported PKI format. It can identify a format, validate a selected format, open format-specific details, or decode the data in the main BerEditor window. Open it from Tool > Check BER.

Figure 1. BER format check dialog. Provide a file or encoded source, identify or select a format, then choose the appropriate check or view action.

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text:
The dialog can identify or check these formats:

  • Certificate
  • CRL (certificate revocation list)
  • CSR (certificate signing request)
  • PublicKey
  • PrivateKey
  • PrivateKeyInfo
  • EncPrivateKey (encrypted private key)
  • CMS
  • PKCS7
  • OCSP response
  • CMP message

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Format list — Shows the formats supported by the checker.
  2. BER file — Select this to use a file as the source. The Find button opens a BER file picker, and the path is shown beside the checkbox.
  3. Source format — When BER file is unchecked, choose how the source text is represented: Hex or Base64.
  4. Source length — Shows the calculated length for the selected source representation.
  5. Source input — Enter or paste the encoded bytes when using text input.
  6. BER Type Check — Detects the source's supported PKI format and selects it in the format list.
  7. Format selector — Choose a specific format to validate or inspect.
  8. Format Check — Checks whether the source conforms to the selected format and reports success or an error.
  9. V — Opens the format-specific information view after validating the selected format. Encrypted private keys require a password.
  10. D — Decodes the source in the main BerEditor window using the selected format title.
  11. Clear — Clears the file path and source text.
  12. Close — Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Check a Source File or Value
docs.text:
1. Choose the source method:
  2. To check a file, select BER file, then select Find and choose the file.
  3. To check encoded text, leave BER file unchecked, select Hex or Base64, and enter the source in the input area.
  4. Select BER Type Check to detect a supported format, or choose the expected format from the format selector.
  5. Select Format Check to validate the source against the selected format.
  6. Read the success message or the reported format error.

docs.title: Open Details or Decode
docs.text:
• After choosing a format, select V to open its detail window. The selected format must pass its format check. Available detail views include certificate, CRL, CSR, public/private key, CMS/PKCS7, OCSP response, and CMP message information.
  • Select D to decode the source in the main BER view. A format must be selected first.
  • For an encrypted private key, V prompts for the password before showing key details.

docs.title: Notes and Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• When using text input, the source must match its selected representation (Hex or Base64). Invalid or empty input cannot be checked.
  • BER Type Check identifies only the formats listed above. If the source is unsupported or malformed, the dialog reports that it could not determine a supported format.
  • Format Check requires a format selection. Choose the expected type or run BER Type Check first.
  • Use Clear before starting a new check to remove the previous file path and source text.

docs.title: BER Compare Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The BER Compare dialog compares two BER files by their encoded bytes and decoded tree structure. Open it from Tool > BER Compare.

Figure 1. BER Compare dialog. Load one file into each side, then compare the structures and inspect matched values.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. SET order support — Enables matching of SET children without relying on their position in the tree. Use this when the order of SET elements should not affect matching.
  2. A File / B File — Shows the selected file path for each side.
  3. Find — Selects a BER file for side A or B and loads its decoded tree.
  4. D — Decodes the corresponding file in BerEditor's main window.
  5. A BER Information / B BER Information — Displays the decoded BER tree for each file. Selecting a node highlights it and its corresponding node on the other side when a match is found.
  6. BER A and B value — Shows the selected nodes' headers and values side by side. If hidden, select Show Value to display this pane.
  7. Status / Compare — Select Compare to compare the loaded BER data. The status reports whether A and B are the same or different.
  8. Clear — Clears both file paths, trees, and value panes.
  9. Show Value — Shows the BER A and B value pane.
  10. Close — Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Compare Two BER Files
docs.text:
1. Select Find on the A File row and choose the first BER file.
  2. Select Find on the B File row and choose the second BER file.
  3. Optionally enable SET order support if SET elements may appear in a different order.
  4. Select Compare.
  5. Read the status message. Matching tree nodes are highlighted; select a node to inspect its corresponding node and value on the other side.

You can also drag and drop two local files onto the dialog. The first file fills A and the second fills B. If both sides are already populated, clear the dialog before dropping different files.

docs.title: Inspect or Decode a File
docs.text:
• Select a node in either tree to display its encoded header and value in the comparison pane.
  • Select D beside a file path to decode that file in the main BerEditor window.
  • If the value pane is not visible, select Show Value.
  • Select Clear before starting another comparison.

docs.title: How Results Are Determined
docs.text:
The dialog first checks whether the complete BER byte sequences are identical. For differing files, it compares nodes by tag, tree depth, definite/indefinite length form, length, and value. A difference in any of these makes the corresponding nodes different. With SET order support enabled, SET children are matched by their parent path rather than their original position.

Both files must be loaded before comparison. If either side is empty, BerEditor asks you to select that file.

docs.title: Binary View Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The Binary View dialog displays binary data as Base64, a formatted hexadecimal dump, or a continuous hexadecimal value. Open it from Tool > Binary View.

Figure 1. Binary View dialog. Base64 is selected by default; use Find to load a file and change the output format as needed.

The implementation file is named bin_view_dlg, while the menu and dialog call this feature Binary View.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Find — Opens a file picker and loads a binary file for viewing.
  2. Base64 — Displays the data as Base64 text. This is the default format.
  3. Hex — Displays a hexadecimal dump in rows of up to 16 bytes.
  4. Raw — Displays the complete hexadecimal value without row formatting.
  5. Address — In Hex view, includes each row's offset. Available only in Hex view.
  6. ASCII — In Hex view, adds printable characters beside each row. Available only in Hex view.
  7. PEM — Wraps Base64 output with BEGIN and END lines. Available only in Base64 view.
  8. PEM type — Selects or enters the label used in the PEM header and footer. The list includes common key, certificate, CSR, CRL, PKCS#7/CMS, and parameter labels.
  9. Output area — Shows the selected representation. It is read-only.
  10. Print / Print Preview — Prints the displayed output or previews it before printing.
  11. Close — Closes the dialog.

docs.title: View Binary Data
docs.text:
1. Select Find and choose a file, or open Binary View from a selected value in BerEditor.
  2. Choose Base64, Hex, or Raw.
  3. For Hex view, optionally enable Address and ASCII.
  4. For Base64 view, optionally enable PEM and choose or enter a PEM type.
  5. Use Print or Print Preview if you need a paper copy.

Display updates automatically when the format or its options change. The data area is read-only. A local file can also be dragged onto the dialog to load it.

docs.title: Format Details
docs.text:
• Base64 output is line-wrapped. With PEM enabled, the selected label is used in the PEM boundary lines.
  • Hex output is grouped into 16-byte rows. Address shows the offset, and ASCII shows printable characters for each row.
  • Raw output is a continuous hexadecimal string; Address and ASCII options are unavailable.

docs.title: BN Calculator Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The BN Calculator performs arbitrary-precision integer and finite-field calculations. Choose a numeric representation and a base group, enter values in A, B, and, when needed, M, then select an operation.

Figure 1. BN Calculator with Hex input and the Number base group selected. Available operations depend on the selected base group.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Numeric type — Choose Binary, Decimal, or Hex. The same representation is used to read inputs and display results. Only digits valid for the selected base are accepted.
  2. Base Group — Choose Number, Modular, or GF2m. This determines which arithmetic operations are available and how the optional M value is used.
  3. A, B, and M fields — Enter operands. M is the modulus used by modular operations; it is disabled when the selected group does not need it. Each section shows the input length and provides its own controls.
  4. C, +1, and -1 — Clear a value or increment/decrement it by one.
  5. Bits, GenPrime, and IsPrime — Choose a bit length and generate a prime for A, B, or M. IsPrime tests the value in that section. Available bit sizes range from 8 to 4096.
  6. Copy / Paste — Copy a value to the clipboard or paste clipboard contents into the field.
  7. Result — Displays the calculation result in the selected numeric type. Send to A, Send to B, and Send to M copy the result into the corresponding operand. Copy copies the result; C clears it.
  8. Timer / Calculation / Sum — Shows the most recent operation and elapsed time in milliseconds. Auto sum adds each operation time to the running total; Add and Sub manually adjust the total. The adjacent C buttons clear the individual time or sum.
  9. Operation buttons — Run arithmetic, modular, bitwise, shift, or number-theory operations. The available buttons and labels vary with Base Group.
  10. Clear All / Close — Clear all operand and result values, or close the dialog.

docs.title: Base Groups and Operations
docs.text: Base Group Operations and behavior Number Standard integer addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, square, remainder, GCD, bitwise OR/AND/XOR/complement, shifts, and prime checks. The modular operand is not used. Modular Arithmetic modulo M, including modular addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, square, shift, inverse, and square root. Operations that require an inverse or square root may fail if the mathematical conditions are not met. GF2m Arithmetic in a binary extension field using the selected field modulus M. Available operations include field addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, square, remainder, inverse, square root, and shifts as enabled in the dialog.

docs.title: Perform a Calculation
docs.text:
1. Select a Numeric type and Base Group.
  2. Enter the required operand values. Use A and B for binary operations; provide M when the selected operation is modular or uses a GF2m modulus.
  3. Select the operation button. The result appears in Result, and the operation time is shown in Timer.
  4. To continue calculating, use Send to A, Send to B, or Send to M to reuse the result as an operand.

docs.title: Generate or Check a Prime
docs.text:
1. In the desired operand section, choose a bit size from Bits.
  2. Select GenPrime to generate a prime and place it in that field.
  3. To test a value already entered, select IsPrime. The result is reported in BerEditor's message/log area.

docs.title: Timing Operations
docs.text:
• Timer displays the latest operation and its elapsed time.
  • Enable Auto sum to add each measured operation time to Sum automatically.
  • Use Add or Sub to adjust the sum by the latest operation time. Clear the latest timer or accumulated sum with its adjacent C button.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Hexadecimal values with an odd number of digits are padded with a leading zero internally for input conversion.
  • Division by zero, invalid modular inverses, and other undefined operations produce a calculation error.
  • In Modular and GF2m groups, select a valid modulus M appropriate to the operation. A generated prime can help create a modulus for prime-field calculations.
  • The GF2m group performs arithmetic over a binary extension field; its operations do not use ordinary integer arithmetic semantics.

docs.title: CAVP Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The CAVP dialog processes cryptographic algorithm test-vector request files and writes response files. It includes symmetric and asymmetric algorithms, hash and MAC tests, Monte Carlo tests, DRBG, PBKDF, and ACVP JSON utilities.

Figure 1. CAVP dialog on the Symmetric Hash tab. Select a request file, configure the matching algorithm and test type, and run the test to create a response file.

docs.title: Shared Control: Rsp Path
docs.text: Rsp Path is the directory where response files are written. Use Find to select a result folder. The dialog remembers this folder. For standard request-file runs, the output is named after the request file with an .rsp extension.

docs.title: Symmetric Hash Tab
docs.text:
This tab contains separate request-file processors:

  • Symmetric — Select a symmetric algorithm, mode (ECB, CBC, CTR, CFB, or OFB), and test type (KAT, MCT, or MMT). Use Find to select the request file and Run to process it.
  • AE — Process authenticated-encryption vectors. Select AES or ARIA, GCM or CCM, and the test type (AE or AD), then choose the request file and run it.
  • Hash — Select a hash algorithm and test type (Short, Long, or Monte), then process the request file.
  • HMAC — Select the hash algorithm used by HMAC, then choose the request file and run it.

docs.title: Asymmetric DRBG PBKDF Tab
docs.text:
• ECC — Select ECDSA or ECDH, a test type, curve parameter, and hash where applicable. Choose the request file and select Run.
  • RSA — Select RSAES or RSA PSS, the test type and hash, and the request file. For deterministic RSA signature tests, use Find DET PrivateKey to supply the private key. E is the RSA public exponent input.
  • DRBG — Process a DRBG request file using CIPHER, Hash, or HMAC method. Select the algorithm and configure Use PR and Use DF as required by the vector set.
  • PBKDF — Select the hash algorithm and process its request file.

Each area has a Find button for the request file and a Run button to generate the response.

docs.title: Monte Carlo Test Tab
docs.text:
• Symmetric MCT — Select algorithm, mode, direction (Encrypt or Decrypt), and count. Enter or inspect the starting Key, IV, PT, and CT, and the corresponding last values. Select Run to generate the Monte Carlo results; Clear resets the fields.
  • Hash MCT — Select the hash algorithm and MCT version (standard or alternate). Enter the count, Seed, and any required First MD / Last MD values, then select Run. Clear resets the fields.

docs.title: DRBG Tab
docs.text: This tab runs a DRBG test from explicit inputs rather than a request file. Select the Method (CIPHER, Hash, or HMAC) and Algorithm, set Rand Len in bits, and choose Use DF and Use PR to match the desired test. Enter the available values as hexadecimal: EntropyInput, Nonce, PersonalString, reseed entropy/additional input, and generation AdditionalInput values. Select Run to display ReturnedBits; Clear resets the inputs and result.

docs.title: ACVP Tab
docs.text:
• ACVP Request Response — Select a JSON request file with Find, then choose Run to generate the response JSON. SetTgId and SetTcId limit processing to the specified test group or test case ID. SkipLDT skips long-duration tests when supported. Clear clears the request path.
  • ACVP Hash LDT — Enter the content (hexadecimal), hash algorithm, and Full Length Bits to hash a repeated content sequence. Run processes it in the foreground. Thread Run starts threaded processing and Thread Stop stops that work. Progress and current processed bit count appear in the status fields; MD displays the digest. Clear resets the LDT fields and progress.

docs.title: Run a Request-File Test
docs.text:
1. Set Rsp Path to the directory where results should be saved.
  2. Open the tab for the test family and select the algorithm, mode, test type, hash, curve, or other options required by the request vectors.
  3. Use Find to select the matching request file.
  4. Select Run. If the request filename does not appear to match the selected algorithm and test settings, the dialog asks you to confirm before continuing.
  5. Review the completion message and the generated .rsp file in the result directory.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Match the selected settings to the request file's algorithm and test type. A mismatch can produce invalid or incomplete response data.
  • CAVP request-file processing and ACVP JSON processing use different tabs and file formats; choose the workflow matching your input.
  • This tool computes responses to test vectors. Running vectors in BerEditor does not itself constitute formal NIST algorithm validation or certification.
  • Protect private-key files used for deterministic RSA tests and keep generated response files with their corresponding request files.

docs.title: Certificate Information
docs.text: The Certificate Information dialog displays the fields and extensions in an X.509 certificate, provides certificate path and status checks, and offers certificate export and management actions.

docs.title: Certificate overview
docs.text: The header identifies the certificate and displays its KID (Key Identifier) when available. The Information tab presents parsed fields in a table. Select a row to see its value in Detail Value. The Field List filter can show all fields, version 1 fields, extensions, critical extensions, or attributes. Use View PubKey to inspect the certificate's public key.

docs.title: Certificate path
docs.text:
The Path Validation tab shows the certificate path tree and related path information. Select a certificate in the tree to inspect it or open its context actions. The available controls include:

Control Description Make Tree Builds a certificate path tree. Cert PVD Runs certificate path validation. Get CA Retrieves the CA certificate associated with this certificate and opens its information. Save to CA Saves the CA certificate to the CA store. Save to Man Saves the certificate to CertMan. Save To RCA Saves the certificate as a trusted root CA. Verify Cert Verifies the certificate signature. CRL Check Checks whether the certificate is revoked using a CRL. OCSP Check Checks certificate status with an OCSP server. OCSP Client Opens the OCSP client. GetURL CA / GetURL CRL Retrieves the CA or CRL distribution URL from the certificate. Get CRL Retrieves the CRL and opens its information. Decode Cert Decodes the certificate in the main BerEditor view.

Some path and CertMan actions are available only in the licensed version.

docs.title: Export and other actions
docs.text:
• Export saves the certificate in PEM format.
  • View PubKey opens the public key information dialog.
  • Close closes the certificate information dialog.

docs.title: Review a certificate
docs.text:
1. Open a certificate in BerEditor's certificate information dialog.
  2. Review its parsed fields in Information. Select fields to inspect their detailed values; adjust Field List to narrow the table.
  3. To inspect trust or revocation, open Path Validation and use Make Tree, Cert PVD, Verify Cert, CRL Check, or OCSP Check as appropriate.
  4. Use Export to save a PEM copy, or Save to Man / CA controls to add it to the relevant store.

docs.title: CertMan Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The Certificate Management dialog organizes certificates, private keys, certificate authorities, CRLs, and trusted root CAs. It also provides common certificate and key operations. The available tabs and actions depend on the selected management mode.

Figure 1. CertMan on the End Entity tab. Select a certificate row to view, export, verify, or use its associated key.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
• End Entity — Manage end-entity certificates and their associated private keys. The table shows subject DN, expiration, and issuer DN. Use the password field when the stored private key is encrypted.
  • Other Cert — Manage additional certificates that are not in the End Entity list; inspect, decode, verify, encrypt to, export, add, or remove them.
  • CA — Manage CA certificates used to build certificate paths. Add, view, decode, export, or remove CA certificates.
  • CRL — Manage certificate revocation lists. Add, view, decode, export, or remove CRLs.
  • Trust RootCA — Manage trusted root certificates, view or export their public keys, load system trust certificates, and remove trust entries.
  • Tools — Work with a private key, certificate, or PFX file. Check key-pair correspondence, inspect key/certificate data, create or extract a PFX, encrypt/decrypt a PFX, and save a PFX entry into End Entity storage.

The screenshots below show the additional tabs and their controls. The certificate paths and certificate names shown are examples from one installation; the contents depend on the local stores.

docs.title: Other Cert
docs.text:
Figure 2. The Other Cert list shows subject DN, expiration date, and issuer DN.

This tab is for certificates kept outside the End Entity store, such as certificates that you need to inspect or use without managing an associated private key here. The key-type filter can narrow the list by algorithm. Select a row to use View Cert, Decode Cert, View PubKey, Export Cert, Run Verify, or Run Encrypt. Add Cert imports a certificate into this store, and Remove Cert removes the selected entry. A row's context menu provides additional actions.

docs.title: CA
docs.text:
Figure 3. CA certificates are listed by subject DN, expiration date, and issuer DN.

Use this tab to maintain intermediate or other CA certificates used by certificate-path workflows. The path field identifies the configured CA store, and the key-type filter narrows the displayed list. Add CA imports a CA certificate; Remove CA removes the selected one. View CA opens its certificate details, Decode CA sends its encoded data to the decoder, View PubKey displays the public key, and Export CA saves the certificate to a file. These actions manage the CA store; they do not themselves assert that a chain is trusted or valid.

docs.title: CRL
docs.text:
Figure 4. The CRL list displays each issuer and its This Update and Next Update dates.

The CRL tab manages Certificate Revocation Lists. The list's update fields help you identify the CRL's stated validity period and freshness. Use Add CRL to import a list, View CRL to inspect its information, Decode CRL to examine its encoded structure, and Export CRL or Remove CRL to save or remove the selected item. Check the issuer and update dates when choosing a CRL; the dates alone do not establish that it is current or applicable to a particular certificate.

docs.title: Trust RootCA
docs.text:
Figure 5. The trust list shows a local name, subject DN, and expiration date for each root certificate.

This tab manages root certificates in the configured trust store. Select an entry to View Trust, View PubKey, Decode Trust, or Export Trust. Add Trust adds a certificate to the store, and Remove Trust removes the selected entry. Load System Trust imports certificates available from the operating system's trust store. Adding a certificate here changes the local trust configuration; only add roots you intend to trust.

docs.title: Tools: private keys and PFX files
docs.text:
Figure 6. The Tools tab accepts a private-key file, a certificate, or a PFX file.

The Tools tab provides a file-based workflow that is separate from selecting an existing End Entity entry:

  • Use Find beside EncPrivateKey, Certificate, or PFX to choose an input file. The small V, C, and D controls beside key and certificate inputs provide view, clear, and decode actions; PFX provides clear and decode controls.
  • Enable Encrypted PrivateKey and enter the private-key password when the selected key file is encrypted. The status line at the bottom reports the key encryption state when known.
  • Choose a PFX encryption mode and provide a PFX password for PFX creation or extraction as required.
  • Check KeyPair checks whether the selected private key matches the public key in the selected certificate. View PubKey and Decode PriKeyInfo help inspect the key material. Get Random generates random data for the workflow.
  • Encrypt PFX packages the selected key and certificate into a PFX file. Decrypt PFX extracts material from a selected PFX. Save PFX to EE imports the PFX contents into End Entity storage.

Use Clear to remove an input from the corresponding field before choosing another file. Treat private keys and PFX files as sensitive material, and protect exported files and passwords accordingly.

docs.title: End Entity Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Certificate Path — Shows the configured End Entity certificate storage folder. The filter can show all entries or narrow the list by key algorithm.
  2. Certificate table — Lists stored end-entity certificates by subject DN, expiration date, and issuer DN. Select a row before using the action buttons.
  3. Password — Enter the password for an encrypted private key associated with the selected certificate when a private-key action requires it.
  4. View Cert / View PriKey / View PubKey — Inspect the selected certificate or its associated private/public key.
  5. Decode Cert / Decode PriKey / Decode PriKey Info — Decode certificate, private-key, or private-key information data in BerEditor.
  6. Check KeyPair — Check whether the selected certificate's public key matches its associated private key.
  7. Run Sign / Run Verify / Run Encrypt / Run Decrypt — Launch the corresponding cryptographic operation using the selected certificate/key material.
  8. Change Passwd — Change the password protecting the selected private key.
  9. Import PFX / Export PFX — Import or export a PFX package containing certificate/key material.
  10. Delete Cert — Remove the selected end-entity entry.
  11. OK / Close — OK confirms a selection when CertMan is opened in a selection mode. Close dismisses the dialog.

The key-type filter can be used to narrow entries to algorithms such as RSA, ECDSA, DSA, SM2, or EdDSA; post-quantum key types may also appear when enabled by the caller. The ALL choice shows entries without an algorithm filter. The certificate table can be sorted by its displayed columns, which is useful when locating a subject or checking expiration and issuer information.

docs.title: Manage Certificates and Revocation Data
docs.text:
1. Choose the relevant tab: End Entity, Other Cert, CA, CRL, or Trust RootCA.
  2. Select a row to enable the actions for that item. Use Add to import an item into the current store, or Remove/Delete to remove it.
  3. Use View, Decode, or Export to inspect or save an item. Right-click a table row for additional item actions.
  4. In End Entity storage, enter the private-key password before using actions that need the private key. Use Check KeyPair to verify that the certificate and private key match.

docs.title: PFX and Tools
docs.text:
• In the Tools tab, choose a private-key file, certificate, or PFX file with Find. Enable Encrypted PrivateKey and enter the password when the private key is protected.
  • Check KeyPair checks whether the selected private key matches the certificate's public key.
  • Encrypt PFX creates a PFX package from a private key and certificate; Decrypt PFX extracts key/certificate files from a PFX. Select an encryption mode and enter the PFX password as required.
  • Save PFX to EE stores the PFX certificate and private key in the End Entity list.
  • Load System Trust imports available system trust certificates into the Trust RootCA store.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The certificate path shown on each tab points to that store's configured directory.
  • Selecting a certificate for an operation may open CertMan in a restricted selection mode. In that mode, double-click a suitable row or select it and confirm with OK.
  • Private-key passwords and PFX passwords protect sensitive key material. Keep them private and verify the selected certificate/key pair before signing or decrypting.

docs.title: Certificate Path Validation Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The Certificate Path Validation dialog helps build and inspect a certificate chain, validate a target certificate, check certificate policies, and verify CRLs. It can use certificates and CRLs selected from files or stored in BerEditor's CertMan lists.

Figure 1. Certificate Path Validation dialog. Supply trust and revocation data, select a target certificate, then build or validate its certificate path.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Use TrustList / Trust List — Enable Use TrustList to validate against BerEditor's configured trust list. Trust List opens CertMan's root CA list. When disabled, provide a specific TrustCert file for the operation.
  2. TrustCert, UntrustCert, and CRL — Select files with Find or choose entries from CertMan with Add. V opens certificate or CRL information; D decodes the selected file in BerEditor. TrustCert supplies trust anchors, UntrustCert supplies certificates treated as untrusted, and CRL supplies revocation information.
  3. Include CertMan CA in UntrustCert — Includes CertMan CA certificates in the untrusted certificate input for path validation.
  4. Path Clear / VerifyCRL / VerifyCert — Path Clear clears the displayed path. VerifyCRL checks a CRL against the selected trust or untrusted certificate. VerifyCert checks the selected certificate using the trust, untrusted, and optional CRL inputs.
  5. At Time / Make Path / Clear — Enable At Time to use the selected date and time for path checks. Make Path builds a chain for the target certificate; Clear clears the path list and tree.
  6. Path List / Path Tree — View the built chain as a table or hierarchical tree. Double-click an entry to view its details. Right-click for available item actions.
  7. Flag Options — Configure certificate-path verification behavior, including CRL checking, policy checks, critical-extension handling, strict X.509 processing, time checks, partial chains, and trust-anchor selection. Use flags only when their validation behavior is intended.
  8. Param — Add verification parameters such as Policy, Purpose, Name, Depth, AuthLevel, HostName, Email, and IP, with a corresponding value. Add appends the selected parameter; Clear removes the parameter list. Right-click table entries for item actions.
  9. Certificate target — Select the target certificate with Find or L (select from CertMan). The subject DN appears in the adjacent field. V views certificate details and D decodes it in BerEditor.
  10. Policy Check / Path Validation — Run a policy check or validate the target's certificate path using the selected inputs, flags, parameters, and time options. Include CertMan CRL in CRL adds CertMan CRLs to path validation.
  11. Clear Data All / Close — Clear the dialog's inputs and results or close the dialog.

docs.title: Build a Certificate Path
docs.text:
1. Select a target certificate using Find or L. The subject DN confirms the selected target.
  2. Enable Use TrustList to use the configured trust list, or select a TrustCert file for a specific trust anchor.
  3. Add any relevant UntrustCert certificates and CRL data. To use CertMan's stored CA or CRL data, enable the applicable inclusion option.
  4. If required, enable At Time and set the validation date and time. Configure any needed verification flags and parameters.
  5. Select Make Path. Review the resulting chain in Path List or Path Tree. When online CA/CRL retrieval is enabled in BerEditor settings, path construction may retrieve issuer or status data online.

docs.title: Validate a Certificate or Check a CRL
docs.text:
• To check the target certificate, select the certificate and configure the trust and revocation inputs, then select VerifyCert. Review the result reported in the log.
  • To verify a CRL, provide a CRL and its issuing certificate as TrustCert or UntrustCert, then select VerifyCRL.
  • To perform full path validation, select Path Validation after setting the target, trust data, optional CRLs, flags, parameters, and time. Use Policy Check when you want to check the configured certificate policy parameters.

docs.title: Verification Flags
docs.text:
The dialog exposes these options (some may be below the visible area depending on window size):

Option Use UseCheckTime / NoCheckTime / At Time Control certificate time evaluation and the selected validation time. CRLCheck / CRLCheckAll Enable CRL checking for certificates in the chain or throughout the chain. IgnoreCritical Ignore unrecognized critical extensions. X509Strict Apply stricter X.509 checks. PolicyCheck / ExplicitPolicy Enable policy processing and explicit policy requirements. InhibitAny / InhibitMap Restrict anyPolicy or policy mapping behavior. PartialChain Allow a chain to terminate at an intermediate certificate. TrustedFirst Prefer trusted certificates when building the chain.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• A successful path depends on a valid target certificate, suitable trust anchors, complete issuer certificates, and any required revocation data.
  • VerifyCert, VerifyCRL, Policy Check, and Path Validation are separate operations and report their results in BerEditor's message/log area.
  • Online retrieval during Make Path follows the online CA/CRL setting configured in BerEditor.

docs.title: CMP Client Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The CMP Client creates and sends Certificate Management Protocol requests for certificate enrollment and management. It supports request types including initial request, certification request, key update, revocation, and general messages.

Figure 1. CMP Client dialog with GENM selected. The enabled credential and request fields depend on the selected command.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. CMP URL — Enter or select the CMP server endpoint. Clear clears the URL history/input.
  2. CA Cert — Select the CA certificate used by CMP. Find, V, D, and T browse, view, decode, or identify the certificate.
  3. Select each certificate and private key — Enable this group to select a client certificate and private key from files; otherwise use CertMan. Enable Enc Private Key and enter its password if the key file is encrypted.
  4. Ref Num / Auth Code — Enter the reference number and authorization code supplied by the CA for enrollment commands that use the out-of-band credentials.
  5. Subject DN — Enter the requested subject distinguished name for IR or CR requests.
  6. GENM / GENP tabs — GENM exposes General Message Information Type and Value (ITAV) options such as CA CERTS, ROOT CA CERT, CERT PROFILE, CURRENT CRL, and SIGN KEY PAIR TYPES. GENP provides general message parameters where available.
  7. Command / Run — Select the CMP operation and choose Run to create the request. Supported commands are GENM, IR, CR, P10CR, SignGENM, KUR, and RR.
  8. Request — Displays the encoded CMP request. Send transmits the request to the CMP URL. C, D, and V clear, decode, or view the request.
  9. Response — Displays the received CMP response. C, D, and V clear, decode, or view it.
  10. Clear All / Close — Clear the dialog or close the client.

docs.title: Create and Send a CMP Request
docs.text:
1. Enter the CMP server URL and select the CA certificate.
  2. Choose a command. For IR or CR, enter the requested Subject DN. For GENM or SignGENM, select the required ITAV options. Enrollment commands may require Ref Num and Auth Code.
  3. For commands requiring an existing identity, enable Select each certificate and private key and choose the matching client certificate/key, or select them from CertMan.
  4. Select Run to create the request. Review it with V or D if needed.
  5. Select Send and review the response. Issued certificate/private-key material may be offered for saving to CertMan.

docs.title: Command Reference
docs.text: Command Purpose GENM Request general information from the CA using selected ITAV values. IR Initial certificate request. CR Request certificate issuance for a subject. P10CR Submit a PKCS #10 certificate request. SignGENM Send a signed general message using client credentials. KUR Request a key update using an existing certificate/key pair. RR Request certificate revocation using the existing certificate/key pair.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The server URL, CA certificate, and command-specific credentials must match the CMP CA configuration.
  • Reference numbers and authorization codes are enrollment secrets; handle them as credentials.
  • A generated request is not sent until Send is selected. Review the response and any certificate/key save prompts.

docs.title: Content Help
docs.text: The Content Help window provides ASN.1 and PKI reference material, RFC documents, and managed web links. Select an item in the information tree to display its content.

docs.title: Main areas
docs.text:
Area Description Information Menu Tree of ASN.1 references, RFCs, PKIX documents, and managed links. The menu can be shown or hidden from the Edit toolbar/menu. Content pane Displays the selected reference, locally available document, or retrieved web content. URI Shows the address associated with the selected online item or the resource path for a built-in reference. Open URI Opens an HTTP or HTTPS address in the system browser.

The tree is populated for licensed installations. RFC and PKIX pages are retrieved from the configured reference sites and cached locally after the first load. Built-in ASN.1 references are loaded from application resources. Managed links are configured through Link Manage.

docs.title: Browse references
docs.text:
1. Expand a category in Information Menu.
  2. Select an item to show its content in the content pane.
  3. For an online reference, review the displayed URI and select Open URI to open it in the system browser.
  4. Use Find to search within the displayed content.

docs.title: Toolbar and menu actions
docs.text:
• Save saves the selected reference to a file.
  • Print and Print Preview print the displayed content.
  • Expand All / Expand Node and Collapse All / Collapse Node control the tree.
  • Show Menu / Hide Menu toggles the information tree.
  • Link Manage opens the link manager for maintaining custom links.
  • Quit closes the Content Help window.

Keyboard shortcuts are shown in the corresponding application menu. The toolbar includes shortcuts for Save (Ctrl+1), Print (Ctrl+2), Expand All (Ctrl+4), Expand Node (Ctrl+5), Collapse All (Ctrl+6), Collapse Node (Ctrl+7), Show Menu (Ctrl+8), Hide Menu (Ctrl+9), and Link Manage (Ctrl+A).

docs.title: CRL Information
docs.text: The CRL Information dialog displays the metadata and revoked-certificate entries in an X.509 Certificate Revocation List (CRL). It also provides signature verification, decoding, export, and CertMan actions.

docs.title: CRL tab
docs.text: The CRL tab lists parsed CRL fields in a Field / Value table. Select a field to view its value in the detail area below the table.

docs.title: Revoke tab
docs.text: The Revoke tab lists revoked certificates by Serial and RevokedDate. Select an entry to display its serial number, revocation date, and available revocation details in the detail table.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Control Description Verify CRL Verifies the CRL signature. Decode CRL Decodes the CRL in the main BerEditor view. Save to CertMan Saves the CRL to CertMan. This control is available in licensed mode. Export Exports the CRL as a PEM file. Close Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Inspect or export a CRL
docs.text:
1. Open a CRL in the CRL Information dialog.
  2. Review the metadata on the CRL tab, or select Revoke to inspect revoked entries.
  3. Select an entry to view its details.
  4. Select Verify CRL to check its signature, or Decode CRL to inspect the encoded structure in the main window.
  5. Select Export to save a PEM copy. In licensed mode, use Save to CertMan to store the CRL there.

docs.title: Decode TTLV
docs.text: The Decode TTLV dialog converts a TTLV message from hexadecimal or Base64 text and opens the decoded structure in BerEditor.

docs.title: Fields and controls
docs.text: Control Description Hex / Base64 Selects how the text in the input area is interpreted. Hex is selected by default. Find Loads a binary data file into the input area using the selected representation. Input area Enter or paste the TTLV message. You can also drop a file onto the dialog. Length Displays the input data length for the selected format. Clear Clears the input area. Decode Parses the input as TTLV and sends the decoded data to the main BerEditor view. Close Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Decode a message
docs.text:
1. Choose Hex or Base64 to match the data you have.
  2. Paste the message, or choose Find to load a file. You may also drop a file into the dialog.
  3. Check the displayed length and select Decode.
  4. Review the decoded TTLV structure in the main window.

If the input is empty or cannot be converted from the selected format, the dialog reports an error and keeps the input available for correction.

docs.title: Document Signer Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The Document Signer handles document signatures, verification, encryption, and data containers in CMS, JSON/JWS, and XML formats. It can work with text in the dialog or read and write source and destination files.

Figure 1. Document Signer on the CMS tab in Encode mode. The JSON and XML tabs provide their own signing, verification, and encryption workflows.

docs.title: Shared Controls
docs.text:
1. Source file / Find — Enable Source file to read the operation's input from a file. Find selects the file; a destination-file control at the bottom can select where to save output. Files may also be dragged into the dialog.
  2. Use CertMan / Use CertMan key — Select whether to use key material from CertMan or, where available, KeyPairMan. The label indicates the active key source.
  3. Use as a template — In XML workflows, use the supplied XML as a template for signing or encryption.
  4. Hash — Select the hash algorithm where applicable.
  5. Clear All / Close — Clear the dialog's input and output fields or close it.

docs.title: CMS Tab
docs.text:
• Source data / CMS data — Enter the content or CMS message. Select the source representation (Hex, String, or Base64). C clears the field; V, D, and T view, decode, or identify CMS data where available.
  • Use TimeStamp / TSP — Attach a timestamp to supported signing operations. TSP configures the timestamp authority/service.
  • CMS Flags — Configure NOVERIFY, NOCERTS, NOSIGS, NOCHAIN, NOINTERN, DETACHED, BINARY, and NOATTR for supported operations.
  • Certificate included in verification — Configure At Time, Certificate, CA List, and TrustList for signed-message verification.
  • Encode / Decode and command — Encode commands include Signed, Enveloped, Add Signed, Data, and Digest. Decode commands include Verify, Developed, GetData, and GetDigest. In Decode mode, Auto Detect dispatches based on the CMS type.
  • CMS data / Source data output — Displays the created CMS message or processed content. View Signer inspects signer information; Export saves the output. The up-arrow copies output into the source field.

docs.title: Create or Process CMS Data
docs.text:
1. Select Encode or Decode and enter source data or load a file.
  2. Select a command. Signed creates signed data; Enveloped encrypts content for a recipient; Add Signed adds a signer; Data wraps data; Digest creates digested data.
  3. For signing or encryption, select the appropriate certificate/key. Choose the hash or cipher when enabled. Set timestamp and verification options as needed.
  4. Select Encode or Decode. In Decode mode, leave Auto Detect on to identify supported CMS types or turn it off to choose a command.
  5. Review the output and use Export or the destination file option to save it.

docs.title: JSON Tab (JWS)
docs.text: The JSON tab works with a JSON payload and a JWS (JSON Web Signature) value. Enter or load the payload, then use Compute Signature to create a JWS or Verify Signature to validate one with the selected key. Check Object checks the JSON object. The payload and JWS controls provide view, clear, copy-to-input (up-arrow), and export actions.

docs.title: XML Tab
docs.text: The XML tab accepts an XML body as text or a source file. Use Check to validate the XML input. Select signing or encryption mode to switch the actions between Make / Verify and Encrypt / Decrypt. The result area displays the generated signature or encrypted XML; use its up-arrow to reuse the result as the next body. Use as a template controls template-based input for XML operations. Select Export to save the result.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• CMS encryption and decryption require a compatible recipient certificate and matching private key. Signing and verification require the appropriate signing key and certificate/trust settings.
  • The Decode Auto Detect feature supports CMS Data, DigestedData, SignedData, and EnvelopedData.
  • JSON signature operations require a compatible key and JWS algorithm. Verify that the key source matches the signing operation.
  • XML signing and encryption require well-formed input; use Check before processing when needed.
  • Protect private keys, passwords, and signed content. Verification outcomes depend on the selected certificate and trust configuration.

docs.title: Encrypt / Decrypt Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The Encrypt / Decrypt dialog performs symmetric encryption or decryption on entered data or a file. Open it from Cryptography > Encrypt/Decrypt.

Figure 1. Encrypt / Decrypt dialog. This view shows input data mode, the AEAD section, and cipher settings.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Input Data / Input File — Enter data directly or select a file to process.
  2. Source data — Choose the input representation and enter or paste data. The Len field reports the decoded length. In file mode, use Find to select the source file and review its size and progress.
  3. Init / Update / Final / Reset — Run the operation incrementally: initialize the cipher, process data blocks with Update, finish with Final, or reset the state.
  4. Key — Select the key representation and enter a key, or leave it blank to choose a symmetric key from Key List. The length is shown beside the field.
  5. IV — Select the IV representation and enter the initialization vector. The note in the dialog describes IV requirements for the selected mode.
  6. AEAD — Enables authenticated encryption modes and associated data controls. Select AAD and enter additional authenticated data. The tag length, tag value, and CCM data length controls are used by the selected AEAD mode.
  7. Encrypt / Decrypt — Choose the operation. The result field is labeled Encrypted data or Decrypted data accordingly.
  8. Algorithm / Mode — Select a symmetric cipher and mode. Available modes depend on whether AEAD is selected and on the chosen algorithm.
  9. Padding — Enables padding where supported by the selected algorithm and mode.
  10. Encrypt / Decrypt button — Runs the selected operation on the current text or file.
  11. Result — Displays the output in the selected representation. The length updates automatically. The up-arrow transfers the output into the input field and selects the matching representation.
  12. Clear Data All / Close — Clears the dialog's data or closes the dialog.

docs.title: Encrypt or Decrypt Text
docs.text:
1. Select Input Data and choose the source data format.
  2. Enter or paste the plaintext (for encryption) or ciphertext (for decryption).
  3. Enter the key and IV, or select a key from Key List when prompted.
  4. Choose Encrypt or Decrypt, then select the algorithm and mode.
  5. For AEAD modes, enable AEAD, provide AAD if required, and set the tag parameters. For CCM, provide the data length requested by the dialog.
  6. Select Encrypt or Decrypt to run the operation.
  7. Review the result. Use the output format selector to view the result as Hex, String, or Base64.

docs.title: Process a File
docs.text:
1. Select Input File, then select Find and choose a source file.
  2. Select or enter a destination file path using the destination-file controls.
  3. Set the key, IV, operation, algorithm, and mode. Configure AEAD options if applicable.
  4. Select Encrypt or Decrypt and monitor progress.

docs.title: Supported Modes and Notes
docs.text:
• Standard modes include CBC, ECB, CTR, CFB, and OFB.
  • When AEAD is enabled, the available authenticated modes include GCM and CCM.
  • ChaCha20 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 have mode and padding controls constrained by the cipher implementation.
  • For AEAD decryption, provide the authentication tag associated with the ciphertext. Authentication failure prevents successful decryption.
  • The input and output fields support Hex, String, and Base64 representations. Ensure the selected representation matches the text entered.

docs.title: Incremental Processing
docs.text: For staged input, select Init, enter a block and select Update for each block, then select Final. The status fields show progress. Select Reset before starting a new operation.

docs.title: EST Client Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The EST Client communicates with an Enrollment over Secure Transport (EST) server to retrieve CA certificates and prepare certificate enrollment requests.

Figure 1. EST Client dialog with the cacerts operation selected. Choose a command, prepare or retrieve its request, send it, and inspect the response.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. EST URL — Enter or select the EST server base URL. Clear clears the saved URL list/input.
  2. CA Cert — Select the CA certificate used for the EST exchange. Find, V, D, and T browse, view, decode, or identify the certificate.
  3. Get CA / Command / Make — Get CA requests CA certificates from the server. Select an EST command and choose Make to prepare a request.
  4. Select each certificate and private key — Enable this group to select client certificate/private-key files directly; otherwise use CertMan. Enable Enc PrivateKey and enter its password if the private key is encrypted.
  5. Request — Displays the prepared EST request. Send transmits it to the server. C clears and D decodes the request.
  6. Response / Verify — Displays the server response. Verify processes/verifies the response as supported by the selected command; C clears and D decodes it.
  7. Clear All / Close — Clear dialog data or close the client.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Purpose cacerts Retrieve the CA certificate collection using Get CA. simpleenroll Create a new key pair and CSR, then prepare a simple enrollment request. simplereenroll Use an existing certificate/key context and prepare a re-enrollment request with a new key/CSR. fullcmc Listed in the command selector; request generation is not implemented in this dialog. serverkeygen Listed in the command selector; request generation is not implemented in this dialog. csrattrs Listed in the command selector; request generation is not implemented in this dialog.

docs.title: Prepare and Send an Enrollment Request
docs.text:
1. Enter the EST server URL and provide the CA certificate where needed.
  2. Select simpleenroll and choose Make. Generate a key pair and complete the CSR information when prompted.
  3. Select Send to submit the request. Review the response in the Response area.
  4. For simplereenroll, select the existing certificate/private key or choose them from CertMan before preparing the request. The client generates a new key and CSR based on the existing certificate identity.
  5. If issued material is returned, follow the prompt to save the private key and certificate to CertMan.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The dialog implementation currently reports fullcmc, serverkeygen, and csrattrs request generation as unsupported.
  • Keep the CA certificate and enrollment credentials consistent with the EST server configuration.
  • Private keys are sensitive. If the selected private key is encrypted, enable Enc PrivateKey and provide its password.

docs.title: Find in BER or TTLV Data
docs.text: The Find dialog searches the currently open BER or TTLV structure for a value. BerEditor enables the matching tab based on the format currently open in the main window.

docs.title: Search options
docs.text: Control Description BER / TTLV tabs Select the data format. The active document determines which tab is available. Header Check Enables the header filters. When unchecked, the search matches values regardless of their headers. Matched Limits the search to an exact value match. Search value Enter the value to find. Value format Selects the input representation. BER searches support String, Hex, Decimal, and OID; TTLV searches support String, Hex, and Decimal. Hex value Shows the converted hexadecimal bytes for the search value. Its length is displayed beside it. Next / Previous Searches forward or backward from the current selection. Edit Opens the selected BER or TTLV node for editing. Close Closes the dialog.

docs.title: BER header filters
docs.text:
With Header Check enabled on the BER tab, configure the optional header criteria:

  • Class: Universal, Application, Content-Specific, or Private.
  • Tag: Select a standard BER tag for Universal class. For other classes, enter a tag ID.
  • Constructed: Match constructed values when selected.
  • Header: Displays the generated one-byte BER header used by the search.

docs.title: TTLV header filters
docs.text: With Header Check enabled on the TTLV tab, enter a six-digit hexadecimal Tag and select a Type. The tag name is shown when recognized. Any searches all TTLV types for that tag; otherwise the generated header includes the selected type.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
1. Open the BER or TTLV data in the main window. The dialog activates the corresponding tab.
  2. Enter the value and choose its format. The hexadecimal representation updates as you type.
  3. Optionally enable Header Check and set BER or TTLV header criteria. Enable Matched for exact matching.
  4. Select Next or Previous to move to a matching node. The node is selected in the main view.
  5. Select Edit to edit the selected node, or Close to dismiss the dialog.

If the value cannot be converted or no matching node exists, BerEditor displays a warning.

docs.title: Hash Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The Hash dialog calculates a digest for text or a file. Open it from Cryptography > Hash.

Figure 1. Hash dialog on the Input Data tab. Select a source, choose a hash algorithm, and select Digest to calculate the digest.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Input Data / Input File — Choose whether to enter data directly or hash a file.
  2. Input Type — Select how the input text is represented (for example, Hex, String, or Base64).
  3. Input area / Input File controls — Enter text in Input Data, or select Find in Input File to choose a file. File mode displays file information, total and read sizes, and progress.
  4. Init / Update / Final — Run a hash incrementally: initialize the selected algorithm, add the current input to the hash state, then finalize and display the digest. Reset clears the incremental operation status.
  5. Status — Shows the state of the incremental operation.
  6. Algorithm — Select the hash algorithm. The list is provided by the application and may depend on the build and crypto configuration.
  7. Request length — Sets the output length for SHAKE128 or SHAKE256. It is disabled for fixed-length hash algorithms. The default is 32 bytes.
  8. Digest — Calculates a one-shot digest for the selected input data or file.
  9. Digest Value — Displays the digest in hexadecimal. Its Len field shows the output length. C clears the digest.
  10. Clear Data All — Clears input, output, and status fields.
  11. Close — Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Calculate a Digest from Text
docs.text:
1. Select Input Data.
  2. Choose the Input Type and enter or paste the data.
  3. Select a hash Algorithm.
  4. For SHAKE128 or SHAKE256, enter the desired Request length in bytes.
  5. Select Digest. The digest appears in hexadecimal in Digest Value.

docs.title: Calculate a Digest from a File
docs.text:
1. Select Input File.
  2. Select Find and choose a file.
  3. Review the file information and select the threading option if shown.
  4. Select Digest and wait for the progress indicator to complete.

The dialog reads the file in blocks and updates the read size and progress. Large files can be processed without loading the entire file into the input text area.

docs.title: Incremental Hashing
docs.text:
Use Init, Update, and Final when you want to feed data to the hash operation in stages:

  1. Select an algorithm and choose Init.
  2. Enter a data block and select Update. Repeat for additional blocks.
  3. Select Final to calculate and display the digest.
  4. Select Reset to clear the operation state before starting another sequence.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The input length and digest length are displayed automatically.
  • Use the same algorithm and input bytes when reproducing or comparing a digest.
  • An empty input is allowed for one-shot digest calculation; it produces the digest of the empty byte sequence.

docs.title: Message Authentication Code (MAC) Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The Message Authentication Code dialog generates or verifies a MAC over text or file data. Open it from Cryptography > Message Authentication Code.

Figure 1. Message Authentication Code dialog. Choose a source, key, method, and algorithm; then generate a MAC or verify a supplied value.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Input Data / Input File — Choose to enter message data directly or select a file.
  2. Input Type — Select the representation for the message input (for example, Hex, String, or Base64). In file mode, Find selects a file and the dialog shows file information and processing progress.
  3. Init / Update / Final / Reset — Provide incremental MAC processing controls. Init starts the operation, Update feeds the current input, Final completes it, and Reset clears the incremental status.
  4. Key value — Enter the MAC key and select its representation. If left empty, the dialog offers the symmetric Key List for selecting a key. The length field is calculated automatically.
  5. IV value — Enter the initialization vector for GMAC. It is disabled for HMAC and CMAC. Select its representation as needed.
  6. Generate / Verify — Select whether to create a MAC or verify an expected MAC value.
  7. Method — Select HMAC, CMAC, or GMAC.
  8. Algorithm — For HMAC, select a hash algorithm. For CMAC and GMAC, select a symmetric cipher algorithm.
  9. MAC / Verify — Runs the selected operation on the current text or file input.
  10. MAC Value — In Generate mode, displays the resulting MAC in hexadecimal. In Verify mode, enter the expected MAC value here as hexadecimal. The Len field shows its length.
  11. Status — Shows Init, Update, and Final results. Reset clears the incremental operation state.
  12. Clear Data All — Clears input, key, IV, output, file information, and status.
  13. Close — Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Generate a MAC from Text
docs.text:
1. Select Input Data and enter the message data using the selected Input Type.
  2. Enter the key and choose its representation, or leave the key empty and select one from the symmetric Key List when prompted.
  3. Select a Method and Algorithm.
  4. For GMAC, enter an IV. HMAC and CMAC do not use the IV field.
  5. Select Generate.
  6. Select MAC. The generated MAC is displayed in hexadecimal in MAC Value.

docs.title: Verify a MAC from Text
docs.text:
1. Enter the message data, key, method, and algorithm as described above.
  2. For GMAC, enter the IV used to generate the expected value.
  3. Select Verify.
  4. Enter the expected MAC in MAC Value as hexadecimal.
  5. Select Verify to calculate and compare the value. The status or message box reports whether verification succeeded.

docs.title: Process a File
docs.text:
1. Select Input File, select Find, and choose the file.
  2. Select the method, algorithm, key, and (for GMAC) IV.
  3. Select Generate or Verify, then select the operation button.
  4. Monitor the progress and read-size indicators while the file is processed.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Algorithm selection IV HMAC Hash algorithm Not used CMAC Symmetric cipher algorithm Not used GMAC Symmetric cipher algorithm Required

docs.title: Incremental Processing and Notes
docs.text:
• Init, Update, and Final can be used to process data in stages. Enter a block in the input area and select Update for each block, then select Final.
  • The key and IV length fields update automatically.
  • Use matching message data, key, method, algorithm, and IV when verifying a MAC.
  • Keep the key secret. Anyone with the key can generate valid MAC values.

docs.title: OTP Generator Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The OTP Generator creates a time-based one-time password (OTP) from a symmetric key, a selected time, a hash algorithm, and a time interval.

Figure 1. OTP Generator dialog. Set the timestamp and OTP parameters, provide the shared key, then generate the code.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Date and Time — Select the timestamp used for generation. Set now fills in the current local time.
  2. Epoch — Shows the selected date and time as Unix time in seconds. It updates when the date/time changes.
  3. Hash — Select the hash algorithm used to generate the OTP. The initial selection follows BerEditor's configured default hash.
  4. Interval — Set the time-step duration in seconds. The default is 60 seconds.
  5. Length — Set the number of decimal digits in the OTP. The default is 6 digits.
  6. Key properties — Select the key representation (Hex, String, or Base64) and enter the shared secret key. The adjacent field shows its length. If the key field is empty when generating, the dialog opens KeyList so you can select a symmetric key.
  7. T value — Displays the time-step value used for this generation, in hexadecimal.
  8. OTP — Displays the generated password as decimal digits.
  9. Gen OTP / Clear Data All / Close — Generate the OTP, clear the key and result fields, or close the dialog.

docs.title: Generate an OTP
docs.text:
1. Set Date and Time, or select Set now to use the current time. Confirm the corresponding Epoch value.
  2. Choose the Hash, Interval, and OTP Length expected by the other system or authenticator.
  3. Enter the shared secret in Key properties and choose its representation. If left blank, select a key from KeyList when prompted.
  4. Select Gen OTP. The time-step value and decimal OTP appear in their result fields.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
