Input Len Read-only length calculated using the selected input format. Clear (input) Clears the input area. Conversion Converts the input to the selected output format. Conversion Format Select the output representation: Hex, String, Base64, URL, or Base64URL. Show printable text For String output, displays printable characters where possible. This option is unavailable for other output formats. Export Opens the export dialog to save the converted output as bytes. Up arrow Copies the current output into the input area and changes the input format to match the selected output format. Output Len Read-only length calculated using the selected output format. Output tab Displays the converted output. Hex Dump tab Displays the converted bytes in a hexadecimal dump with printable characters. Clear (output) Clears the output and hex dump. Close Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Convert Data
docs.text:
1. Enter or paste data in the input area, or select Read File to load a file.
  2. Select the matching input format. For example, choose Hex for hexadecimal text or Base64 for Base64 text.
  3. Select the desired Conversion Format.
  4. If the output format is String, optionally select Show printable text.
  5. Select Conversion.
  6. Review the result in the Output tab. Select Hex Dump to inspect the underlying bytes.

The input and output length fields update as the text or format changes. If no input is provided, BerEditor asks you to enter a value. Invalid input for the selected format produces a format error.

docs.title: Load a File
docs.text:
1. Select Read File.
  2. Choose a file in the file picker.
  3. BerEditor loads the file bytes into the input area as hexadecimal data and selects Hex as the input format.
  4. Choose an output format and select Conversion.

The file loader accepts files up to 1 MB. Dragging a local file onto the dialog also loads its contents as hexadecimal input.

docs.title: Use the Output as New Input
docs.text: Select the up arrow beside the output format controls. The output text is copied to the input area, and the input format is set to the currently selected output format. The existing output and hex dump are cleared so you can perform another conversion.

docs.title: Export Converted Data
docs.text: Select Export to open the export dialog for the converted output. Export is available when the output area contains data. The displayed output is decoded according to the selected output format before it is passed to the export dialog.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• URL and Base64URL are separate formats. Select the one that matches the input or desired output.
  • Show printable text changes String output rendering; it is disabled for other output formats.
  • The Hex Dump view shows bytes in 16-byte rows and includes printable characters where available.
  • The dialog's output format initially defaults to Base64.

docs.title: Decode BER Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The Decode BER dialog converts BER data entered as text into bytes and loads it into BerEditor for decoding. Open it from Tool > Decode BER.

Figure 1. Decode BER dialog. The format controls and file picker are above the input area; Clear, Decode, and Close are along the bottom.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Input format — Choose Hex, Base64, or Base64URL. The selected option determines how BerEditor interprets the text in the input area.
  2. Find — Opens a file picker to load a BER file into the input area.
  3. Len — Shows the calculated data length for the current input and format. This field is read-only.
  4. Input area — Enter or paste the encoded data. Its placeholder indicates the selected format.
  5. Clear — Removes the text from the input area.
  6. Decode — Decodes the input and loads it into the main BerEditor window.
  7. Close — Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Dialog Controls
docs.text: Control Description Hex Treats the input as hexadecimal data. This is the default format. Base64 Treats the input as Base64 data. The input may also be a PEM value. Base64URL Treats the input as URL-safe Base64 data. Input area Enter or paste the encoded data here. The placeholder changes with the selected format. Len Displays the calculated data length for the current format. It is read-only. Find Selects a BER file and loads its contents into the input area using the selected format. Clear Clears the input area. Decode Decodes the entered data and loads it into the main BerEditor window. Close Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Decode Data
docs.text:
1. Open Tool > Decode BER.
  2. Select the input format: Hex, Base64, or Base64URL.
  3. Enter or paste the encoded data into the input area.
  4. Review the value shown in Len.
  5. Select Decode.

When decoding succeeds, the dialog closes and BerEditor displays the decoded data in the main window. If the input area is empty, the application asks you to enter data. If the data cannot be parsed in the selected format, a format error is displayed.

docs.title: Load Data from a File
docs.text:
1. Select the desired input format.
  2. Select Find and choose a BER file.
  3. The file contents are placed in the input area in the selected format.
  4. Select Decode to load the data into the main window.

The file picker checks that the selected file can be read as BER data. If it is not a valid BER file, BerEditor displays an error.

docs.title: Drag and Drop
docs.text: You can drag a local file onto the dialog to load it into the input area. The dialog converts the file contents to the currently selected representation: hexadecimal, Base64, or Base64URL. Then select Decode to inspect the data.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Make sure the selected format matches the text you entered. For example, choose Base64URL for URL-safe Base64 text.
  • Use Clear before entering a different value if you want to avoid mixing it with existing input.
  • Len is calculated from the selected encoding; it is not an editable field.
  • The dialog processes BER data. Other data formats may produce a decoding or format error.

docs.title: BerEditor Main Window UI Guide
docs.text: Figure 1. The supplied image currently shows the Data Converter dialog. The main-window layout described below is based on the application source code.

docs.title: Main Window Layout
docs.text:
The main window is divided into a left BER tree pane and a right workspace. The right workspace has an upper data viewer and a lower information/log panel. Splitters let the user adjust the pane sizes.

Area Description Menu bar Provides File, Edit, Tool, Cryptography, Service, Protocol, KMIP, Help, and View commands. Toolbars Optional toolbars provide shortcuts to commands from the menus. Which toolbars and buttons appear can be configured in View. BER tree (left) Displays the decoded BER structure as a navigable tree. Select a node to inspect its data and details. Data viewer (upper right) Shows the selected data in Hex, XML, Text, or JSON tabs. The Hex view is displayed as a table with an address, byte columns, and printable text. Information (lower right) Shows details about the currently selected node or data. Log (lower right) Shows application messages and operation output. Status bar Displays status information when an operation provides it.

Some data-view tabs and the Log tab may be unavailable depending on license status. The exact presentation can also vary by platform and window size.

docs.title: Menus
docs.text:
Menu Main purpose File Create a new window; open BER, certificate, CRL, CSR, key, or CMS data; save; view recent files; print; and quit. Edit Copy selected information as-is, Hex, or Base64; expand or collapse tree nodes; navigate between nodes; and find a node. Tool Decode BER; convert data or numbers; inspect OIDs; create or check BER; retrieve BER from a URI; compare BER; and open binary/text views. Cryptography Manage keys and perform hash, MAC, encryption, signature, key agreement, PKCS#7, secret sharing, certificate path validation, OTP, VID, and big-number operations. Service Manage key pairs, certificates, and keys; check SSL/TLS; compare X.509 certificates; sign documents; and access CAVP tools. PDF signing appears when enabled in the build. Protocol Open clients for OCSP, TSP, CMP, SCEP, ACME, and EST. KMIP Decode, create, encode, or send KMIP TTLV messages. Help Configure settings; clear or pause logging; open PKI content, license information, support links, and About information. View Configure which toolbar actions are shown and restore the default view configuration.

For the full command list and shortcuts, see Menu Guide.

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
1. Use File > Open... to open a BER file, or choose the appropriate specialized open command for a certificate, CRL, CSR, key, or CMS file.
  2. Select a node in the BER tree on the left.
  3. Inspect the selected data in the Hex, XML, Text, or JSON viewer tabs on the right.
  4. Read node details in Information and operation messages in Log.
  5. Use File > Save or File > Save As... when you need to save the current BER data.

docs.title: Resizing and View Options
docs.text:
• Drag the divider between the tree and right workspace to change their relative widths.
  • Drag the divider between the upper data viewer and lower Information/Log panel to change their heights.
  • Use the View menu to show or hide toolbar actions and Set Default to restore the configured default view.
  • If an expected action or data tab is unavailable, check the license status and the current View configuration.

docs.title: File
docs.text: Menu item Description New Opens a new BerEditor window. Open... Opens a BER file. Open Certificate Opens a certificate file. Open CRL Opens a certificate revocation list (CRL) file. Open CSR Opens a certificate signing request (CSR) file. Open PrivateKey Opens a private key file. Open PublicKey Opens a public key file. Open CMS Opens a CMS file. Save / Save As... Saves the current data or saves it under another name. Recent Files Reopens a recently used file. Up to 10 entries are maintained. Print / Print Preview Prints the current content or previews it before printing. Quit Exits BerEditor.

docs.title: Edit
docs.text: Menu item Description Copy Information Copies the contents of the current selection to the clipboard. Copy As Hex Copies the selected value in hexadecimal format. Copy As Base64 Copies the selected value in Base64 format. Expand All / Expand Node Expands all nodes in the BER tree or the selected node. Collapse All / Collapse Node Collapses all nodes in the BER tree or the selected node. Previous Node / Next Node Moves to the previous or next node in the tree. Find Searches for a node in the BER data.

docs.title: Tool
docs.text: Menu item Description Decode BER Decodes BER data. Data Converter Converts data character encodings or representations. Num Converter Converts numeric representations. OID Information Looks up Object Identifier (OID) information. Make BER Creates BER data. Check BER Checks the format and validity of BER data. Get BER from URI Retrieves BER data from a URI. BER Compare Compares two BER data values. Binary View / Text View Opens data in binary or text view.

docs.title: Cryptography
docs.text: Menu item Description Key Manage Provides key derivation and key encryption/decryption functions. Hash Generates a hash value. Message Authentication Code Generates a message authentication code (MAC). Encrypt/Decrypt Encrypts or decrypts data. Sign/Verify Creates or verifies a digital signature. PubKey Encrypt/Decrypt Encrypts or decrypts data using a public key. Key Agreement Performs DH or ECDH key agreement. PKCS7 Creates and validates PKCS#7 messages. Shamir Secret Sharing Splits a key or combines key shares. Certificate Path Validation Validates a certificate path. OTP Generator Generates a one-time password (OTP). VID Generates and validates VID values. BN Calculator Performs big number calculations. Make PrivateKey Generates a private key.

docs.title: Service
docs.text: Menu item Description KeyPair Manage Lists and manages asymmetric key pairs. Certificate Manage Lists and manages certificates and keys. Key List Lists and manages symmetric keys. SSL Check Checks SSL/TLS protocol connections. X509 Compare Compares X.509 information. Document Signer Provides document digital signing functions. PDF Signer Provides PDF digital signing functions. Availability depends on build options. CAVP Provides cryptographic algorithm validation functions.

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text: Menu item Description OCSP client Checks certificate status using OCSP. TSP client Processes Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP) requests. CMP client Processes Certificate Management Protocol (CMP) requests. SCEP client Processes SCEP certificate enrollment requests. ACME client Processes ACME protocol requests. EST client Processes EST protocol requests.

docs.title: KMIP
docs.text: Menu item Description Decode TTLV Decodes KMIP TTLV messages. Make TTLV Creates KMIP TTLV messages. TTLV Encoder Encodes TTLV messages. TTLV Client Runs the KMIP TTLV client.

docs.title: Help
docs.text: Menu item Description Settings Configures the application environment. Clear Log Clears messages in the Log tab. Log Pauses or resumes logging. Content Displays PKI-related information. License Information Displays license and registration information. Bug or Issue Report Reports bugs or issues. Q and A Opens question-and-answer information. About BerEditor Displays information about BerEditor.

docs.title: Number Converter Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The Number Converter converts a number between binary, decimal, and hexadecimal representations. Open it from Tool > Num Converter.

Figure 1. Number Converter dialog. Enter a value at the top; the equivalent values appear in the three output sections below.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Number Type — Select the radix of the value entered in the input field: Bit (base 2), Decimal (base 10), or Hex (base 16). Decimal is selected by default.
  2. Input field — Enter the value to convert. The placeholder indicates valid characters for the selected type.
  3. Input Clear — Clears the input field.
  4. Binary output — Shows the equivalent binary representation. Its length is shown in the small read-only field beside the up-arrow button.
  5. Decimal output — Shows the equivalent decimal representation and its length.
  6. Hex output — Shows the equivalent hexadecimal representation and its length.
  7. Up-arrow buttons — Copy that section's value to the input field and select its matching input type, allowing conversion from that representation.
  8. Output Clear — Clears all three converted values and their lengths.
  9. Close — Closes the dialog.

docs.title: Convert a Number
docs.text:
1. Select the input Number Type.
  2. Enter a value in the input field.
  3. Read the equivalent values in the Binary, Decimal, and Hex sections. Conversion occurs as you type.
  4. To use one of the results as the next input, select the up-arrow button beside that result.

docs.title: Input Formats
docs.text:
Type Valid digits Example Bit 0 and 1 101101 Decimal Decimal digits; a minus sign is supported for negative values 45 or -12 Hex 0–9, A–F, or a–f 2D or a4

Whitespace is removed before conversion. An invalid value triggers a warning. When entering hexadecimal with an odd number of digits, the converter pads a leading zero internally before decoding it.

docs.title: Clear Values
docs.text:
• Select the top Clear button to clear the input field.
  • Select the bottom Clear button to clear the Binary, Decimal, and Hex results.

docs.title: OID Information Dialog Guide
docs.text:
The OID Information dialog looks up Object Identifier (OID) details from an OID or one of its supported representations. Open it from Tool > OID Information.

Figure 1. OID Information dialog. Choose an input representation and enter its value; the matching fields are populated as you type.

docs.title: Screen Areas
docs.text:
1. Input type — Select the representation of the value to search for.
  2. Input field — Enter the value. The placeholder text changes to indicate the expected input.
  3. OID — Displays the dotted-decimal object identifier.
  4. OID Value Hex — Displays the hexadecimal encoding of the OID value.
  5. OID Hex — Displays the BER-encoded OID in hexadecimal form.
  6. Short Name — Displays the OID's short name, when available.
  7. Long Name — Displays the OID's long name, when available.
  8. Nid — Displays the numeric identifier (NID), when available.
  9. Clear — Clears the displayed result fields.
  10. Close — Closes the dialog.

The lookup runs as you type or change the input type. The result fields are read-only.

docs.title: Supported Input Types
docs.text: Input type What to enter Example format OID Dotted-decimal OID 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1 OIDValueHex Hexadecimal OID value bytes Hexadecimal characters, for example 2A864886F70D010101 OIDHex BER-encoded OID bytes in hexadecimal Hexadecimal characters, for example 06092A864886F70D010101 ShortName OID short name For example, rsaEncryption LongName OID long name Enter the name used by the OID database. Nid Numeric identifier A numeric NID value.

docs.title: Look Up an OID
docs.text:
1. Choose the appropriate input type from the selector.
  2. Enter or paste the corresponding value in the input field.
  3. Read the resolved OID and any available associated values below.
  4. Select Clear to clear the result fields before another lookup, or replace the input to search again.

If a name or NID is not known to the OID database, some result fields may remain blank. The dialog does not provide a separate Search button; lookup is triggered by changes to the input.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• OIDValueHex and OIDHex are different: OIDHex includes the BER tag and length bytes, while OIDValueHex contains the OID value bytes.
  • Short name, long name, and NID are shown only when the underlying OID database has corresponding entries.
  • The dialog also contains a Create action in the UI definition, but it is hidden by the current application implementation; it is therefore not part of the visible workflow shown above.
